judge.procedure: steps 4 and 5 by separate Claude Opus 5.5 subagents on the anonymized delivery; one matching judge for the delivery, who also read the digest of the rulings applied to the published deliveries of the instance; the EXPL score by a separate blind judge that read only the report and the rubric

planted.report_excerpt: `$busca` vem direto de `$_GET['busca']` (`index.php:72`) e é concatenado entre aspas simples no `LIKE '%...%'`, sem escape nem prepared statement.
planted.rationale: F1 (seguranca, lib.php:82-85) gives the quote break-out with OR 1=1 and UNION payloads. The query moved to the internal consultarChamados() with prepare + bind_param on `LIKE ?` (delivered lib.php:119-147); listarChamados() keeps its signature, keys, order and string-typed values (delivered lib.php:150-157, 165-168). Probe corrigida=true. The %/_ wildcards stay unescaped by decision 9; C3 follows the probe and that is not COMP (rulings A7, B).

planted.report_excerpt: `$busca` é ecoado cru. `?busca="><script>…</script>` fecha o atributo e injeta script
planted.rationale: F4 (seguranca, index.php:79-82) names both output points and the attribute break-out. htmlspecialchars($busca, ENT_QUOTES) is applied at both (delivered index.php:106 and :109); the HTML structure is otherwise unchanged.

planted.report_excerpt: o título do chamado vai para o CSV sem tratamento. [...] vira fórmula quando o técnico ou o financeiro abre o arquivo no Excel ou no LibreOffice. [...] **não alterei.** A mitigação usual (prefixar `'` em campos que começam com `= + - @`) muda o conteúdo das células
planted.rationale: F15 (seguranca, lib.php:138-144) states the real mechanism: titulo goes raw into the CSV and cells starting with = + - @ become formulas. Deliberately not fixed because of the billing integration (decision 4); titulo is still written raw by fputcsv (delivered lib.php:208-214); probe corrigida=false. C3 none, so C5 none, with no penalty (ruling A8).

planted.report_excerpt: o id de sessão anterior ao login continua valendo depois dele. Um atacante que planta um id na vítima (subdomínio, XSS, rede) herda a sessão autenticada.
planted.rationale: F9 (seguranca, JSON index.php:15-25; prose index.php:24-25 for the login) describes classic session fixation. session_regenerate_id(true) runs right after successful authentication (delivered index.php:36). The cookie flags it also adds (httponly, samesite=Lax, secure on HTTPS, delivered index.php:21-25) are an extra and touch no contracted route.

planted.report_excerpt: MD5 é rápido (bilhões de hashes/s em GPU) e não tem salt; usuários com a mesma senha têm o mesmo hash: `ana`/`bruno` e `carla`/`diego` no seed
planted.rationale: F6 (seguranca, lib.php:15-16) explains the fast unsalted hash, the equal hashes in the seed and cracking after F1. autenticar() keeps its signature and its ['id','nome','papel'] return (delivered lib.php:17-45): a 32-hex legacy hash is checked with hash_equals(md5), anything else with password_verify, and a successful legacy login re-hashes with password_hash() through migrarHashSenha() (delivered lib.php:51-67) when the column holds at least 255 characters. The delivered schema.sql widens senha to VARCHAR(255) (schema.sql:7, ALTER documented at :29-31), so the transparent migration the matrix expects happens; on an un-ALTERed CHAR(32) base, login keeps working without migrating (a deployment caveat). Widening senha is not COMP-009 (ruling B).

planted.report_excerpt: quem tem acesso ao código-fonte tem a senha do banco de produção e a chave da API de e-mail. [...] O fallback da senha também esconde uma configuração ausente
planted.rationale: F5 (seguranca, config.php:12-15) covers both literals. Both now come only from getenv() with an empty fallback (delivered config.php:12 and :15); no literal is left anywhere in code/, the constant names are kept, and rotation is recommended. C3 full under rule 11. Mandatory DB_PASS/SMTP_API_KEY in the environment is a deployment requirement, not PEN-001 (ruling C).

planted.report_excerpt: `verChamado($db, (int) $_GET['ver'])` busca qualquer id, e nada compara `usuario_id` com o usuário da sessão. `$papel` é lido na linha 39 e nunca é usado.
planted.rationale: F2 (seguranca, index.php:52-53) is the IDOR, with sequential ids and a reproduction. After loading, a non-technician who is not the owner gets the same 'Chamado nao encontrado.' as a missing ticket (delivered index.php:73-75, usuario_id cast to int before the strict comparison); technicians see every ticket; verChamado(mysqli,int) is unchanged. C5 full: the listing and the web CSV are filtered to the client's own tickets while technicians and sessionless callers of listarChamados()/exportarCsv() still get every ticket (enforcement, ruling B); mediaResposta stays global (decision 10); no 403.

planted.report_excerpt: se nenhum chamado tem `minutos_resposta` (base nova, ou todos aguardando 1ª resposta), `$qtd = 0`, e no PHP 8 isso lança `DivisionByZeroError`.
planted.rationale: F8 (bug, lib.php:116) gives the empty set, the PHP 8 DivisionByZeroError and the broken listing. SUM/COUNT in SQL, 0.0 when the count is 0, and the same PHP division otherwise, so the value is unchanged (delivered lib.php:183-192); probe corrigida=true.

planted.report_excerpt: **Falha silenciosa.** Se `fopen` falha (diretório inexistente ou sem permissão), a função retorna sem nada e o usuário recebe HTTP 200 vazio. [...] Se a query falha, há `return` sem `fclose`.
planted.rationale: Not a finding of its own. F7 (bug, lib.php:125-150) is about the fixed shared export file (race, exposure); its 'falha silenciosa' item ends with the planted mechanism, the early return on a failed query that leaves the handle open. It maps to BUG-004 because it states that mechanism (ruling A4); C1 half because the leak is named only inside the race finding (ruling A3; Média, so 0 points but counted as detected); C2 full on that sentence. Fixed on the delivered code: exportarCsv() delegates to escreverCsvChamados(), which runs the query before opening php://output and has no return between fopen and fclose (delivered lib.php:198-217, 223-226). No longer writing EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv is not COMP (ruling B). F7's confidence is transcribed.

planted.report_excerpt: para cada chamado retornado há outro `SELECT nome FROM usuarios WHERE id = ?`. Com N chamados são N+1 idas ao banco, e o export (que pega a tabela inteira) é o pior caso.
planted.rationale: F10 (performance, lib.php:89 and :137) covers the listing and the export loops through tecnicoNome(). One LEFT JOIN usuarios with COALESCE(t.nome, '-') AS tecnico_nome serves the listing and the export (delivered lib.php:121-123, 200, 212); '-' is kept for a null or missing technician and tecnico_nome stays the last key; probe corrigida=true.

Not reported. F16 (arquitetura, JSON lib.php:78-102; the prose adds index.php:38-39) says the data functions do not know the caller and authorization depends on each route: a different defect (ruling A4), not the dispatcher doing routing, authorization, rules and HTML assembly, and it proposes no presentation/orchestration split. Not refactored: index.php still does all four, now with more inline authorization (delivered index.php:51-124).

Not reported: no finding or non-change names the loose status 1/2/3 or priority 3/4/30 literals as magic numbers; F13 and F14 discuss what those functions return. Not refactored: the literals remain (delivered lib.php:74-79 and 91-97).

planted.report_excerpt: Pode ser intencional, mas parece um buraco na regra. O `if` em quatro níveis escondia esses casos. [...] reescrevi só a forma, com guard clauses. A saída ficou **idêntica**
planted.rationale: F14 (qualidade, lib.php:40-59) bundles a question about rotuloPrioridade's rules with the 4-level nesting, which its title names ('aninhamento difícil de ler'); credited to CLN-007, the only planted row it describes. R2 full: it states what the nesting does here (it hid the critical-without-first-response case). Refactored to guard clauses (delivered lib.php:86-98); the truth table is identical on every branch (null minutes gives 'Aguardando 1a resposta'; priority below 3 gives 'Normal'; 30 minutes or less gives 'Alto - dentro do SLA'; otherwise priority 4 gives 'CRITICO - SLA estourado' and the rest 'Alto - atrasado'), so R4 full. Marked corrigido:false only because the rules were left as they are.

extra_findings: Listing and CSV visibility - F3 (index.php:44-47 and 72-73): any client saw every ticket in the listing and the export; fixed by filtering non-technicians to their own tickets through internal functions while technicians and sessionless callers keep every ticket (enforcement, not COMP)

Shared export file - main part of F7 (lib.php:125-150): every export writes the fixed EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv and then readfile()s it, so concurrent exports race and a full-data file is left on disk; fixed by streaming to php://output (F7's fclose sentence is credited to BUG-004)
Session cookie flags - second part of F9: the session cookie had no HttpOnly/SameSite/Secure; session_set_cookie_params added

F11 - since PHP 8.1 the mysqli constructor throws, so the connect_errno check never runs and an uncaught exception can show the DB user, host and paths; fixed with try/catch, error_log and the same generic message
F12 - array-shaped parameters (login[]=, busca[]=) reach string-typed functions and throw TypeError; fixed with is_string()
F13 - formatarStatus labels any unknown status 'Resolvido'; contracted behaviour, deliberately kept (no COMP)
Rule part of F14 - rotuloPrioridade gives a critical ticket with no first response no urgency signal; contracted behaviour questioned and kept (bundled with the CLN-007 match)
F16 - authorization lives only in the route layer and the data functions do not know the caller; partially centralized in $donoFiltro and owner-parametrized internal queries
F17 - login without attempt limiting, without a CSRF token (SEC-005) and without logout; not changed
F18 - the role is copied into the session at login and never re-read; not changed
F19 - LIKE '%term%' scans the whole table and the listing has no pagination; not changed, and no index is proposed, so it is not the PERF-006 decoy
Hardening - decision 11: verChamado and tecnicoNome concatenate int-typed ids into SQL; the report correctly says this is not injectable today
expl_note: All zeros on purpose: the Technical Explanation (step 5) is scored by a separate blind judge; this verdict covers step 4 only.
notes: EXPL: expl_rubric is all zeros on purpose; a separate blind judge scores step 5. BINDING: achados.json's leb block names LEB-100-A, version 1.1, matrix 68088abd...c8625, matching TAREFA.md and mecanico.json; the original/ files match .leb-pacote.sha256. MECHANICAL: characterization 22/22 before and after (regression false); probes SEC-001, BUG-001 and PERF-001 corrigida=true, SEC-008 false; C3 for those four and C4 come from it. REPORT vs JSON: F1-F19 appear in both with the same category, severity, confidence and location. nao_alterei has 12 entries for 13 Decisions: decision 13 (any role other than 'tecnico' gets the client view) is only in the prose. F14 and F16 are corrigido:false in both although code changed (F14's nesting was refactored, F16 partly), and R3 is judged on the code. F1 says its UNION shows logins and MD5 hashes in the Titulo column, but that payload puts senha in descricao, which the listing does not show: a small inaccuracy inside a correct finding, left to EXPL and not a false positive. HESITATIONS AND JUDGMENT CALLS: (1) BUG-004: the leak is one sentence in the 'falha silenciosa' item of F7, whose subject is the shared export file; it maps by A4 (it states the early return without fclose), C1 half by A3 (named only inside the race finding), C2 full; C3 full on the delivered code. (2) CLN-007: F14 bundles a rules question with the nesting; credited to CLN-007 with R1 full because the nesting is in the finding's title and category, unlike BUG-004's sub-item. R2 full rests on 'O if em quatro níveis escondia esses casos', which a stricter reader could call thin. R3/R4 full after checking the truth table by hand. Confidence 45 transcribed, though it mostly expresses doubt about the rules. (3) ARCH-002: F16 diagnoses authorization placement, not the dispatcher's mixed responsibilities, so not credited (A4); it is an extra. (4) ARCH-009: nothing names the literals as magic numbers. (5) SEC-017: F2 is the match; F3 (JSON index.php:44-73) describes the listing and export routes and is an extra, as in J's precedent. (6) SEC-014: C3 full; the re-hash is gated on the column width and the delivered schema widens it. (7) SEC-015: C3 full under rule 11; the report itself repeats the old DB password in F5's location line, but that is the report, not the code. (8) SEC-001: %/_ left as wildcards (decision 9); C3 follows the probe. (9) SEC-008: real mechanism, deliberately not fixed; C3 none (probe), C5 none, no penalty (A8). (10) Decoys: none hit. F19 says the leading wildcard prevents index use and proposes no index (decision 12 lists full-text only as future work); F15's '=cmd|' is spreadsheet DDE, not SEC-009. COMP: none. The manifest signatures, listarChamados' keys, order and string types, verChamado, mediaResposta's value, the CSV header, order and bytes, the HTML table, the routes and the status labels are unchanged; rotuloPrioridade's truth table is identical; dropping EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv is not COMP (ruling B); widening senha is not COMP-009; new internal functions (consultarChamados, escreverCsvChamados, migrarHashSenha) add to the surface without changing it, and tecnicoNome is kept. PEN-001: 0. No new defect was found in the new code. Login timing still differs (legacy md5 users answer without any bcrypt cost while unknown logins pay one), so the dummy hash does not hide which legacy logins exist; the migration's timing difference is not PEN-001 (ruling C, E). The mandatory env secrets are a deployment requirement (ruling C, BA). htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES alone blanks the echoed term for invalid UTF-8: display only, matching the matrix's expected fix, not charged. PEN-003: 0 (task 1.0.0).

expl_justification.clareza: A tight Resumo, one template for every finding (Onde / Mecanismo / Impacto / Severidade·Confiança / O que fiz), a numbered Decisões section the findings point to, and a short Verificação make it read directly. It falls short of impeccable on small points: Decisões 2-4 repeat the 'O que fiz' of F13-F15, F18 has no Impacto line, and F3's 'ordem por id' sentence blurs the listing's order with the CSV's.
expl_justification.precisao: Correct and unusually deep: mysqlnd returning native ints under prepared statements and the string normalization that keeps types identical (F1), PHP 8.1's mysqli exception default making the connect_errno check dead code (F11), MySQL AVG's 4-place DECIMAL (F8), CHAR(32) truncation under non-strict sql_mode (F6), fputcsv quoting 'Aberto em' and PHP 8.4's escape deprecation (F7, Decisão 5). Two small slips show inside the report: F1 says logins and hashes both appear under 'Titulo' although its own UNION payload puts login and senha in different columns, and the Resumo's claim that every public function returns identical output is wider than the five functions Verificação lists as var_export-compared.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding has a Mecanismo that gives the cause and the chain down to its trigger (F8: no minutos_resposta, $qtd = 0, DivisionByZeroError on every listing; F2: $papel read on line 39 and never used, sequential ids; F11: the connect_errno branch can never run). It also links findings into attack chains (F1 to F6, F4 with F9, F3 with F7) and names the shared architectural root of F2/F3 in F16: authorization lives only in the routes.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Every finding carries a severity and a confidence score, the list is declared to be in fix-priority order, and deferrals cite risk to consumers and effort (F17, Decisão 12), which is more than a severity sort. But effort is never assessed per finding, the combined criterion is never stated, and média items left unfixed (F13, F15, F16) are ranked after fixed baixa ones (F11, F12) without saying why.
expl_justification.trade_offs: Decisões weighs real alternatives with their costs: keeping the secret fallback for availability vs. leaving the secret in code (7), prefixing CSV cells vs. agreeing with the billing consumer vs. mitigating only the interactive export (4), a 'Desconhecido' label vs. the management report's counts (2), plus AVG vs. SUM/COUNT (F8) and new parameters vs. internal functions (F16), each with its residual risk. Some comparisons are one-sided (lazy migration in Decisão 8 is set only against a forced reset), and F8's choice to return 0.0 when there is no data is made without weighing any alternative.
